content.text: Each polyfill uncovers another Node core module. Before adding more, I'll check why a browser bundle needs jsonwebtoken at all.

content.content:
src/client/auth/session.ts:1:import jwt from 'jsonwebtoken'
src/server/auth/issue.ts:2:import jwt from 'jsonwebtoken'

content.text: Root cause: the client only calls jwt.decode(), which needs no crypto, but importing jsonwebtoken drags its whole Node-only dependency tree (jws, crypto, stream, buffer) into the browser bundle. Webpack 4 hid that with automatic polyfills; webpack 5 doesn't. Better fix than polyfills: decode in the client with jwt-decode (browser-native, ~1 KB) and keep jsonwebtoken server-side only.

messages.content: Agreed, no polyfills. Keep the bundle small, it's already over our 450 KB budget.

input.command: git checkout webpack.config.js && npm uninstall crypto-browserify stream-browserify util

content.text: 'not.a.jwt' base64-decodes to something JSON.parse accepts in jsdom's atob, so jwt-decode returns an object without claims. readClaims should also reject a payload with no string `sub`.
